  Full text: MIT filmed the man who ran its AI Lab teaching what artificial intelligence actually is, 12 years before the current boom. Almost nobody watches it. This is 6.034, Artificial Intelligence, lecture 1, taught by Patrick Winston. He directed the MIT AI Laboratory from 1972 to 1997, taking over from Marvin Minsky. He studied under Minsky himself. Lecture 1 is definition and history. Not code, not frameworks. What the field claimed it was doing, what it got wrong, and how many times it already declared victory too early. Watch the first 15 minutes. He gives a definition of intelligence that no product demo in 2026 can satisfy, and he does it without a single slide. Skip the last 10 minutes, that part is course admin for students who were in the room. An AI engineer I know rewatched the opening twice and said it reframed everything his team was building. Full course free on YouTube under Creative Commons. The field is 70 years old. Most people arrived last year.
